items.text: Selection methods · Fetchers · Spiders · Proxy Rotation · CLI · MCP Scrapling is a Python Web Scraping framework that brings fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, powerful parsing, and concurrent crawling into one library. Scrape static pages, render JavaScript, interact with websites, and extract data from the API calls behind them. Build crawlers with reusable sessions, proxy rotation, automatic retries, pause/resume, and built-in data exports. Use it from Python, the terminal, or your AI agent through its MCP server and Agent Skill. From extracting a few fields to collecting a whole website as clean Markdown, Scrapling covers the full scraping workflow. - Fetch & interact: Fast HTTP requests, stealth browsers, JavaScript rendering, Cloudflare Turnstile/Interstitial handling, persistent sessions, and background API capture. - Parse & extract: CSS, XPath, text and regex search, adaptive element tracking, similar-element matching, and clean Markdown output. - Crawl & export: Concurrent spiders, proxy rotation, retries, AutoThrottle, pause/resume, streaming, ready-made templates, and JSON/JSONL/CSV/XML exports. - Scrape with AI or from your terminal: An MCP server for AI agents to browse and extract data, an Agent Skill, CLI commands, and an interactive shell. Start with a single page: from scrapling.fetchers import Fetcher page = Fetcher.get('https://quotes.toscrape.com/') quotes = page.css('.quote .text::text').getall() print(quotes) Or scale up with a spider: from scrapling.spiders import Spider, Response class QuotesSpider(Spider): name = "quotes" start_urls = ["https://quotes.toscrape.com/"] async def parse(self, response: Response): for quote in response.css('.quote'): yield { "text": quote.css('.text::text').get(), "author": quote.css('.author::text').get(), } res...

items.text: 让 AI Agent 够得着它自己上不去的互联网 让你的 Agent 直接搜索和阅读 X、Reddit、YouTube、小红书…… 💬 有问题、想要新平台、或者想看看别人怎么用？来 Discord 聊聊。 点击展开 Agent Reach 让你的 Agent 真正连上互联网，用上它自己够不着的平台和能力。 Claude Code、Codex、Hermes Agent、OpenClaw 这类 CLI Agent 自带搜索和网页读取，但下面这些它们基本够不着： - 要登录才能用的功能：在小红书搜笔记、在 X 查账号动态、读职位详情等。 - 视频里的内容：B站和 YouTube 的字幕，以及 YouTube 视频、小宇宙播客的语音转文字。 - 中文平台：B站、小红书、V2EX、雪球，通用搜索覆盖很差。 - 干净的结构化数据：雪球行情、V2EX 帖子和回复、GitHub 仓库和 issue，拿到的是整理好的内容。 Agent Reach 把这些平台背后的工具替你装好、测好，Agent 一条命令就能用： agent-reach channels # 有哪些渠道、每个渠道能做什么 agent-reach bilibili search "大模型" # agent-reach [参数] agent-reach read https://www.v2ex.com/t/123 # 按链接自动选渠道 - 适用于哪些 Agent？ 一切 Agent 都能用。 - 会碰我的浏览器和账号吗？ 要登录的平台用 Agent Reach 自己的专用浏览器，在后台运行、不弹窗。第一次用某个网站时，会把你 Chrome 里这个网站的登录复制一份过去，原浏览器不变，不读密码库。复制过来的通常是主账号，建议换成小号，做法见下面的"安全性"。详见会话配置。 下表是当前版本的情况。 - 默认：装好就能用；不想要也可以去掉，以后更新不会再加回来。 - 可选：说一句"帮我加上 XX"就开启，需要的软件会自动装好。 - 实验：能用，但平台反爬更严，可能随时失效。 把这句话发给你的 Agent： 帮我安装 Agent Reach：https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Panniantong/Agent-Reach/main/docs/install.md 无论是安装还是升级，都只需要这一条命令就行了。 剩下的 Agent 自己做完。过程中你可能会被问到： - 允许它执行命令：如果 Agent 说自己不能运行命令，去它的设置里打开"允许执行命令"。 - 装 uv：uv 是一个安装命令行程序的小工具，不需要管理员密码。电脑上没有的话 Agent 会先装它，会跟你说一声。 - 要不要加可选渠道：装完后 Agent 会告诉你哪些已经能用（B站、V2EX、GitHub、YouTube、网页），以及还能加哪些。你选了再加，也可以以后随时说"帮我加上小红书"，一条命令就装好。 关于登录：部分平台会直接复用你电脑上已有的登录。想换成某个特定账号（比如小号），跟 Agent 说一声就行。Agent 从不替你登录，也不会要你的密码。 ⚠️ PyPI 上叫agent-reach 的包不是本项目，请勿从 PyPI 安装，只用 install.md 里的 GitHub 地址。 Agent Reach 装的所有东西（各渠道的工具、登录、设置）都放在你电脑上同一个文件夹里（~/.agent-reach/ ），不散落到别处。所以升级、管理、删除都很省事，一句话就行。 直接用大白话跟 Agent 说： 出了问题，Agent 会告诉你是哪个平台、什么原因、下一步怎么做。常见问题见 troubleshooting.md。 每个平台的每个动作都有一个按顺序尝试的工具列表。比如读 B站视频先用 bili-cli，失败了自动换 B站公开接口；读网页先用 Jina Reader，再用 Exa。 flowchart LR A[Agent] -->|agent-reach 渠道 动作| B[Agent Reach] B --> C{按顺序尝试} C -->|首选| D[上游工具 1] C -->|失败时备选| E[上游工具 2] D --> F[结果] E --> F F --> A 平台改版、工具失效是...

items.text: 伯乐Skill（Scout Skill）帮你从一堆信源里选出千里马。 AI News Radar 是一个自动更新的 24 小时 AI 更新雷达。 普通用户直接打开网页，看最近 24 小时 AI、模型、开发者工具和技术生态更新。维护者可以 fork 这个仓库，接入自己的 OPML/RSS、公开 feed、静态页面或 AgentMail 邮箱情报。Codex / Claude Code 这类 Agent 可以使用项目内置的 伯乐Skill，继续帮你判断信息源、维护抓取逻辑、部署 GitHub Pages。 这个项目不是“又一个新闻网页”。 它的核心是伯乐Skill，帮你从一堆信源里选出千里马。哪些源值得长期追踪，哪些源适合做成RSS/OPML，哪些源只能接付费的API，哪些源看起来更新很多但实际上跟你长期关注的方面比方AI只占了里面的5%不到。 先判断清楚，再接入。 好新闻分散在各处， 官方博客发一点，更新日志发一点，X 上有人提前爆料，聚合站又把同一个新闻转来转去。 我以为的自己在追前沿，实际每天都在重复三件事， 打开几十个页面，肉眼+人脑过滤重复内容，猜哪条值得看。 伯乐Skill先替你完成第一轮判断，哪些信源是千里马，哪些是噪音。 你可以随意增加信息源，还可以把一个信息源纳入输入范围，先让它在单独的展示区域运行一个月，再判断要不要录入。 AI News Radar从来都不是单纯把信息抓回来， 它更像是一条轻量的新闻pipeline，把来源判断、抓取、去重、AI强相关过滤、信息源健康状态和静态网页发布串起来，上线后不消耗模型额度。 - 追踪官方 AI 节点，OpenAI News、OpenAI Codex Changelog、OpenAI Skills、Anthropic、Google DeepMind、Google AI、Hugging Face、GitHub AI 等 - 读取高信号日报和Newsletter公开来源，例如 AI Breakfast - 读取网页自带的feed，例如 Follow Builders 的 X builders、Anthropic Engineering、Claude Blog、AI podcasts - 同时接入多个公开聚合源，例如 AI HOT，补足普通官方源看不到的盲区 - 支持OPML/RSS批量导入 - 支持AgentMail邮箱订阅高质量AI日报 - 输出24小时双视图， AI强相关 和全量 - 中英双语标题和站点分组 - 兼容飞书文档，追加了WaytoAGI开源社区最近更新日和近7日变化 flowchart LR source["信息源清单"] --> classify["伯乐Skill判断信源类型"] classify --> official["官方 RSS / changelog"] classify --> opml["私人 OPML / RSS"] classify --> publicFeed["公开 GitHub feed / JSON"] classify --> staticPage["公开页面 / Jina 兜底"] classify --> privateMail["AgentMail 邮箱订阅"] classify --> skip["跳过高风险来源"] official --> fetch["抓取与结构化"] opml --> fetch publicFeed --> fetch staticPage --> fetch privateMail --> fetch fetch --> dedup["去重与归一化"] dedup --> filter["AI 强相关过滤"] filter --> status["源健康与覆盖统计"] filter --> data["data/*.json"] status --> data data --> pages["GitHub Pages 网页"] data --> agent["Codex / Claude Code 继续维护"] AI News Radar学习了现代新闻学的技术，不是简单堆信息源，一次性放几万条信息出来等于没用，所以我选择把新闻处理拆成稳定pipeline，抓取，去重，过滤，补充状态，生成静态站点。 在...

items.title: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo
items.summary: OpenAI and Cisco introduce Shirudo, an open-source runtime for Linux. It helps teams protect running systems while they roll out patches.
items.text: An open-source runtime that helps operators protect running Linux systems without needing to wait for the patch or restarts OpenAI and Cisco are launching Shirudo, an open-source runtime that helps teams protect Linux systems while they roll out patches. In a controlled test(opens in a new window), a Codex-generated shield blocked a Java4Shell exploit attempt against a running Elasticsearch service without requiring a restart. We’re inviting developers, security researchers, and infrastructure operators across the industry to help develop the project further. The project brings together OpenAI’s frontier AI, security and infrastructure research and Cisco’s infrastructure and security expertise to help protect the systems people rely on every day. Testing and deploying a patch can still take days or weeks. Protecting a service in the meantime can be challenging because an exploit and a legitimate request may rely on the same Linux operation. Blocking that operation entirely could take the service offline. Shirudo (Japanese for “shield”) is designed to help security teams navigate this tradeoff. Teams can test whether a temporary safeguard, called a shield, blocks the behavior that exposes a vulnerability while allowing legitimate requests through. Once an operator approves the shield, it can be deployed while the service continues running. How Shirudo works Shirudo uses eBPF, a Linux technology that allows small programs to run at specific points inside the operating system. This makes it possible to observe suspicious activity and apply targeted security protections to running systems. OpenAI and Cisco are designing Shirudo around four core capabilities: Live protection: eBPF shields can block vulnerable code paths without restarting the system. Security teams can monit...

items.title: datasette-charts 0.2a0
items.summary: Release: datasette-charts 0.2a0 I introduced this new charting plugin for Datasette yesterday . Today it's gained integration with Datasette Agent , so now you can ask chat for a chart and it will create one for you using the same underlying chart suggestion and generation tools. Here's a demo video, recorded on agent.datasette.io where you can sign in with GitHub to try the plugin yourself: Download the video (MP4) I prompt Datasette Agent to "Use #stats to show sqlite-utils downloads over time as a chart" - where typing "#stats" opens a table search box. It shows me a chart inline in the chat, and when I click "Open in the chart builder" it opens the chart in a panel along with the table page. I use the table page to switch to a chart of "datasette", then when I ask the agent "what does the chart show?" it notices that I changed the content in the panel and describes the new Datasette chart to me. Here's a Markdown export of the chat from the video. Tags: datasette-agent , datasette , visualization

items.summary: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count. This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th, who said: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. GLM 5.4 is not (yet?) available as open weights. I tried it out using the Z.ai API, for which I had to sign up for their Coding Plan subscription because 5.4 cannot currently be accessed through the regular API. items.summary: Release: datasette-charts 0.1a0 I've been thinking about this problem for over a year now, but on Sunday I finally fired up Claude Fable 5.2 to build an initial prototype. The prototype went so well that this is now a full plugin. You can try it out in Datasette Lite here . It looks like this: The new charts plugin works against any table or arbitrary SQL query in Datasette. It defines several different chart types (using vendored D3 , Observable Plot , and topojson-client ), each with a set of heuristics for identifying when they might be a good match for a specific set of rows. Those suggestion thumbnails at the top are actual visualizations driven by the data, and selecting one pulls up the full chart along with tools for modifying it. You can also manually construct a chart from scratch. As with other Datasette visualization plugins, the current state of your chart is persisted in a #fragment in the URL - so you can bookmark charts or share them with others. The most important feature is that the charts take all rows into account . Previous charting plugins like datasette-vega would only show charts for the current page of results, generally up to 100 rows. The new plugin compi...

As with other Datasette visualization plugins, the current state of your chart is persisted in a #fragment in the URL - so you can bookmark charts or share them with others. The most important feature is that the charts take all rows into account. Previous charting plugins like datasette-vega would only show charts for the current page of results, generally up to 100 rows. The new plugin compiles each chart to a SQL query that aggregates across the entire result set (potentially millions of rows) using GROUP BY, time bucketing, and window functions. Each query returns a result capped at 5,000 rows, suitable for display on the chart. The plugin uses sampling to help suggest charts for larger tables without evaluating the full result set. I'm really happy with this initial release of the plugin. It's still very much an alpha, but it's the closest I've got to the dream of Datasette helping visualize data with as little required direction from the user as possible. items.text: Maintainers don’t need more AI bug reports. They need fixes. In the Codename MDASH pilot, GitHub and Microsoft turned thousands of raw AI findings into 99 checked, private reports with suggested fixes for six widely used open source projects. Maintainers have already fixed more than half. AI has made finding potential vulnerabilities fast and cheap. Fixing them still takes human judgment, and in open source, that work falls to maintainers. Many are already flooded with AI-generated security findings, including duplicates and reports that aren’t vulnerabilities at all. Another raw scan doesn’t help them. Anyone pointing a new model at a project should ask its maintainers first and come with fixes, not just findings. AI shouldn’t add to maintainers’ workload. So, with maintainers, GitHub and Microsoft ran a pilot together: could AI help maintainers ship fixes instead of handing them more findings? GitHub and Microsoft are using Codename MDASH, Microsoft’s multi-model agentic scanning harness, to find and fix security vulnerabilities in widely used open source software, strengthening the foundation that much of the world’s code is built on. The process Our pilot had two goals: send only findings that matter, and never send a maintainer an unverified finding. Here’s how it worked: Find.Codename MDASH, an AI system from Microsoft Security, scanned each project using Microsoft’s MAI Cyber model and suggested fixes for what it found. Filter. An AI triage agent from the GitHub Security Lab, built on tailored Copilot skills, removed duplicates, checked validity, and focused on high-impact bugs, so maintainers never had to review raw scan results. items.summary: Comments
items.text: I, too, can make a chart of perplexity drops Today, OpenAI released a blog post showing the perplexity of their models over time. The drop is impressive, and the claim is that perplexity itself can be a universal measure of intelligence. After seeing this chart, the thought that came to mind was: perplexity against what? Perplexity is a measure of how well token likelihoods predict the actual next token. Perplexity is meaningless without knowing what text the model is trying to predict. The answer was buried in a footnote. The chart is based on models predicting a fixed corpus of code. So the problem here is obvious. Could this chart just be a reflection of OpenAI models being increasingly trained on code? Keeping the model the same but changing the training mix I set about investigating this. My plan was to find an open source repo with a tiny model and a documented training set, then monkey with it. While getting started, my agent found an existing paper that already did this. (The agent was Astra 6.2, funny enough. It must have low perplexity on this kind of tomfoolery.) The authors of the paper ran five training sets on a 160M model, varying only the proportion of the training data that was code. Here is what they found: Spoiler: the “internal model” here is the same 160M model with 75% of the training corpus being code. As expected, if you look at perplexity on non-code text, it increases dramatically: Conclusions Obviously, the model here with 75% code in the training corpus almost certainly is smarter at code. The point here isn’t that OpenAI’s chart measures nothing, only that their post should have a lot more qualifications [1]. items.title: Perplexity and Intelligence
items.summary: How perplexity measures progress in AI models, and why it could help developers establish a shared approach to evaluating emerging capabilities.
items.text: From afar, it might seem like modern AI is built similarly to how software has been built in previous decades: with a diverse set of techniques targeting specific capabilities. There are indeed a variety of methods, but rather than designing something from scratch, they are mostly harnessing the intelligence coming from a much simpler and less interpretable process: training a compressor (or, equivalently(opens in a new window), predictor) on a very large corpus of data.1 I believe tracking the pace of progress on training better compressors is key to understanding the arc of advances in AI. In this post, I argue for establishing perplexity (or, equivalently, cross-entropy loss) as a metric to compare between model developers and inform shared safety standards. As a first step, I provide more transparency into pretraining progress at OpenAI. Publishing our internal perplexity measurements took some consideration; it gives competitors a clearer picture of where we stand, but that concern is outweighed by the urgency of establishing shared(opens in a new window) safety measures across the industry. We at OpenAI hope for this to be a step towards building a shared scientific basis for future pacing efforts. A simplified, but fundamentally informative, view of AI development is that first, one builds a large computer, then uses it to pretrain a model (compressor) on a large unstructured dataset, then applies a variety of techniques—like prompting, finetuning or reinforcement learning—in different contexts to elicit the latent capabilities of that model. Today we are releasing Stalwart 1.2.0, and with it Stalwart becomes a drop-in replacement for Microsoft Exchange. Stalwart now implements the protocols that Exchange clients speak: MAPI over HTTP, Exchange Web Services (EWS), Exchange ActiveSync and Autodiscover. Outlook, Apple Mail and the mail apps on phones and tablets connect to Stalwart as they would to an Exchange server, with mail, calendars, contacts, tasks and notes in one account. Exchange support is part of the open source Community edition, under the AGPL. Before going into what Stalwart now does, it is worth looking at where self-hosted Exchange stands today, because it explains why so many organisations are looking for a way out. Microsoft has not announced the end of Exchange Server. On paper, on-premises Exchange still exists. In practice, every road Microsoft is building leads to Exchange Online: - Exchange 2016 and 2019 are out of support. Both reached end of support on 14 October 2025. items.text: India's opposition storms Meta's offices to get its Instagram accounts back Last Friday, activists from the Indian Youth Congress, the youth wing of India's main opposition party, forced their way into the building housing Meta's offices in Hyderabad, where they ended up clashing with police among overturned potted plants. The scene repeated itself the same day in Mumbai, with anti-Meta slogans spray-painted on the building's walls and placards burned in front of the entrance, while in Gurugram, near New Delhi, banners demanded the return of the movement's accounts. Mumbai police registered a complaint against four of the organization's leaders and detained several protesters. This anger stems from the November 19 blocking of the Instagram accounts of the youth wing's president and of the party official who oversees it. The Congress accuses Meta of obeying orders from the BJP, Narendra Modi's Hindu nationalist party, and of restricting, along the way, thousands of accounts belonging to journalists, creators and influencers critical of those in power. The movement had warned on X that it would storm the company's offices across the country if the accounts weren't reinstated. Promise kept, then. And the method pays off, since two accounts were restored the day after the protests, according to the group's social media chief, who is now giving Meta seven days to lift all restrictions targeting opposition voices. Meta restricted more than 5.4 million posts or accounts in India in the first half of 2026, compared with around 70,000 over the whole of 2025. The government, for its part, issued almost 200,000 blocking orders between March and July, and since February has required platforms to remove flagged content within three hours, compared with 36 previously. items.title: New York Bans Subscription and Post-Purchase Fees on Cars
items.summary: Comments
items.text: S.9348A/A.10411A Prohibits Car Companies from Charging for Built-In Features Amid Rising Consumer Fees, New Law Increases Price Transparency and Puts Money Back in New Yorkers’ Pockets Governor Kathy Hochul today signed a bill restricting motor vehicle manufacturers and dealers from charging consumers subscription fees after they purchase a vehicle. Amid rising consumer prices, the new law guards against a rising trend of car companies charging car owners fees to activate and use built-in features like heated seats, enhanced navigation, hands-free driving and entertainment options that do not present an ongoing expense for dealers and manufacturers. “New Yorkers are already struggling with rising prices due to Trump’s affordability crisis, and we’re not going to let harmful business practices increase the cost of living even more,” Governor Hochul said. “People spending their hard-earned money on a car shouldn’t have to fork over even more money for features that should automatically come with the car. My message to car companies is clear: this kind of deceptive business model isn’t going to fly in New York State. Keep your hands out of New Yorkers’ wallets.” S.9348A/A.10411A prohibits motor vehicle manufacturers, dealers or third-party service providers from adding subscription services or charging post-purchase fees for any motor vehicle feature that uses pre-installed components or hardware that do not have an ongoing cost. As vehicles become more advanced, the new law aims to establish clear rules preventing exploitative practices and prevent post-purchase fees as a future automotive business model.
